Documentation → Other Products → FortiADC → New virtual server (guided)

Guided virtual server wizard (FortiADC)

Build a complete FortiADC load-balancing chain — real servers, pool, pool members and virtual server — from one form, with a preview of every REST call and automatic rollback if a step fails.

👤 ForOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsnetwork.view network.edit network.apply
📍 WhereFortiADC ADOM → FortiADC → Server Load Balance → Virtual Server → Wizard (URL /adc/wizard/virtual-server)

What is it?#

A FortiADC virtual server cannot exist without a load-balance pool, and the pool needs at least one real server as a member. The guided wizard collects everything in one form and creates the objects in the right order: real servers → pool → members → virtual server. Nothing touches the device until you click Create all.

What does it do?#

  • Validates the form before talking to the device (names, IP addresses, at least one back-end, unique back-end names).
  • Checks that none of the virtual server, pool or real server names already exist on the device.
  • Preview plan lists every REST call it would send, with method, path and body.
  • Create all sends the calls one by one. If a call fails, it deletes, in reverse order, the objects this run already created.
  • Offers the device's interfaces, application profiles and load-balancing methods as suggestions in the form.

Requirements#

  • A FortiADC selected in the ADOM. Without one, the wizard redirects to the FortiADC dashboard.
  • Names that are not yet used on the device.

Permissions#

Action Permission
Open the wizard page The legacy view gate, which any read permission grants (for example network.view)
Preview plan and Create all Any key that grants configuration writes, for example network.edit or network.apply

The Wizard button on the Virtual Server page (and New (guided) on the classic page) is only shown to users with write permission. Without it, both buttons of the wizard fail with HTTP 403.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 3.1.0: the wizard opens from the Wizard button of the measured FortiADC → Server Load Balance → Virtual Server page. The classic Virtual Server page, with its New (guided) button, is no longer in the sidebar; an old address reaches it with ?classic=1.

How to use#

  1. Go to FortiADC → Server Load Balance → Virtual Server and click Wizard.
  2. Under Virtual server, fill in Name, Pool name (new), IP address (VIP) and Port, and choose Status.
  3. Check Interface, Profile and LB method. Start typing to see the values the device already has.
  4. Under Real servers (back-ends), enter Name, IP address, Port and Weight for each back-end. Click Add server for more rows; the x button removes a row. Rows left completely blank are ignored.
  5. Click Preview plan. The right-hand card shows Plan — N REST call(s) and ends with Nothing sent yet — click Create all to apply.
  6. Click Create all and confirm Create the pool, real servers and virtual server on the device now?
  7. On success the card shows Virtual server <name> and N object(s) created. Click See it in the list.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Name Virtual server name Yes vs-web-prod
Pool name (new) Name of the pool the wizard creates Yes pool-web-prod
IP address (VIP) Virtual IP; must be a valid IPv4 or IPv6 address Yes 192.0.2.50
Port Virtual server port No (default 80) 443
Status enable or disable for the virtual server No (default enable) enable
Interface FortiADC interface No (default port1) port1
Profile Application profile No (default LB_PROF_TCP) LB_PROF_HTTP
LB method Load-balancing method No (default LB_METHOD_ROUND_ROBIN) LB_METHOD_ROUND_ROBIN
Real server Name Back-end object name, unique within the form Yes, per row rs-web-1
Real server IP address Back-end IP Yes, per row 192.0.2.51
Real server Port Port used by the pool member No (default 80) 8080
Real server Weight Pool member weight No (default 1) 1

Real servers and pool members are always created with status enable. Members are numbered 1, 2, … in the order of the rows.

The wizard does not fill in or check names against the FortiADC patterns on the Naming page; those patterns are reference only.

Example#

🧪Example — Two back-ends behind one VIP

  • Name vs-shop, Pool name pool-shop, IP 192.0.2.80, Port 443, Profile LB_PROF_HTTP.
  • Back-ends rs-shop-1 / 192.0.2.81 / 8443 and rs-shop-2 / 192.0.2.82 / 8443.

Preview plan shows six calls: two real servers, the pool, two pool members (?pkey=pool-shop) and the virtual server. Create all creates them in that order.

Result#

  • The objects exist on the device immediately.
  • One audit entry adc.wizard_create is written for the virtual server, with the number of objects created.
  • The wizard writes no audit entry for a failed run; the response lists what was created and what was rolled back.

Troubleshooting#

"Already on the device: … — pick different names."#

Possible causes — one of the names (virtual server, pool or a real server) already exists on the device.

Solution — change the listed names, or create only the missing pieces in the object editor.

Verification — Preview plan shows the plan.

"Cannot proceed" with a list of errors#

Possible causes — validation failed. The messages are, for example, Virtual server name is required., Pool name is required., Virtual server IP address is required., Virtual server IP "…" is not a valid IP., Real server #2: IP address is required., At least one real server (back-end) is required. or Real server names must be unique within the batch.

Solution — correct the fields named in the messages.

Verification — the card title changes to Plan — N REST call(s).

"Failed at: …" after Create all#

Possible causes — the device refused one call (for example an unknown profile or interface). The card shows the failed step, the device error and Rolled back: … with the objects that were removed again.

Solution 1. Read the device error and fix the value (profile, method, interface…). 2. Check the list on the device: rollback is best effort, so an object whose delete also failed is not listed under Rolled back. 3. Run the wizard again.

Verification — Create all ends with the Created card.

Advanced#

Advanced Order and rollback

The plan is built without any device access. On Create all the wizard first lists each object type once to detect name conflicts (HTTP 409 when it finds one), then creates each step in order. On the first failure it deletes what it created in reverse order (pool members with ?pkey=), ignoring delete errors, and returns HTTP 502 with failed_step, created and rolled_back.

#fortiadc#virtual server#wizard#pool#real server#rollback
